requirements: Reproduce R²CCL, a fault-tolerant collective communication library that provides lossless failover via multi-NIC hardware for LLM training and inference, matching the paper's claimed overheads and speedups over baselines.

sub_tasks.requirements: Hardware, software, and simulator environments required to reproduce R²CCL experiments are correctly provisioned.
The physical two-node H100 testbed hardware and interconnect are provisioned as described.
The testbed consists of exactly two server nodes interconnected via InfiniBand fabric, matching the configuration used for all physical-testbed experiments.

verification.spec: Inspect the testbed configuration/launch scripts or environment manifest to confirm exactly two server nodes are used, connected via InfiniBand. Verify by parsing hostfile/MPI config or reading NCCL topology output showing 2 distinct nodes with IB HCAs. Fail if node count != 2 or if interconnect is not InfiniBand.

sub_tasks.requirements: Each server node is equipped with 8 NVIDIA H100-80GB SXM5 GPUs, and this is confirmed via nvidia-smi or equivalent detection in the setup scripts/logs.

verification.spec: Run `nvidia-smi -L` on each of the two nodes and parse the output; assert 8 GPUs are listed per node and every entry's product string contains 'H100 80GB' and 'SXM'. Also parse `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total --format=csv` and assert memory.total is ~81559 MiB.

sub_tasks.requirements: Each server node has 8 NVIDIA ConnectX-7 400Gbps InfiniBand NICs, with all 8 detected and usable for RDMA traffic.

verification.spec: Run `ibstat` and `ibv_devinfo` on each node and assert 8 ConnectX-7 InfiniBand HCAs are present with active link state and 400 Gbps (NDR) rate. Verify each is usable for RDMA by launching `ib_write_bw` on each device index.

sub_tasks.requirements: Intra-node GPUs are connected via NVLink 4.0 delivering 900GB/s bidirectional bandwidth, verified through NVLink topology query (e.g., nvidia-smi topo -m) or a bandwidth microbenchmark.

verification.spec: Run `nvidia-smi topo -m` and confirm all intra-node GPU pairs report NV# (NVLink) connectivity. Additionally run NCCL-tests `all_reduce_perf` single-node 8-GPU with 1GB payload and confirm measured bus bandwidth exceeds 700 GB/s, consistent with NVLink 4.0 900 GB/s bidirectional capacity.

sub_tasks.requirements: NVIDIA SHARP is explicitly disabled in all experiments (e.g., NCCL_ALGO does not select SHARP; NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=0), and this is documented in the run configuration.

verification.spec: Grep launch scripts and confirm NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=0 (or SHARP explicitly disabled via NCCL_ALGO not including CollNet/SHARP). Run a small NCCL AllReduce with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and grep the log for 'SHARP' or 'CollNet' — must NOT appear as an active algorithm/plugin.

sub_tasks.requirements: The software stack (compilers, NCCL version, PyTorch, vLLM, NCCL-tests) is built at the exact versions specified in the paper.
NCCL is built from source at version 2.23.4, and the resulting library reports this version at runtime.

verification.spec: Build NCCL from source at tag v2.23.4. At runtime, call ncclGetVersion() (or read from NCCL_DEBUG=VERSION output) and assert the reported version equals 22304 (encoded 2.23.4). Also confirm the resulting libnccl.so.2.23.4 shared library exists.

sub_tasks.requirements: PyTorch v2.10.0 is compiled against NCCL 2.23.4 (and separately against R²CCL) for the training experiments, producing importable modules that link to the correct NCCL build.

verification.spec: Build PyTorch v2.10.0 from source linked against the two NCCL builds (vanilla 2.23.4 and R2CCL). After each build: `python -c 'import torch; print(torch.__version__); print(torch.cuda.nccl.version())'` — assert torch is 2.10.0 and NCCL version matches the linked library. Confirm both variants are importable.

sub_tasks.requirements: vLLM v1 is built on top of NCCL 2.23.4 and R²CCL for the inference experiments, with the resulting binary able to launch the v1 engine.

verification.spec: Build vLLM v1 twice: once against vanilla NCCL 2.23.4 and once against R2CCL. Confirm each build's `vllm --version` reports v1 engine. Launch a minimal `vllm serve` with tensor_parallel_size=2 for a small model and confirm the engine reaches the READY state, exercising the linked collective library.

sub_tasks.requirements: NCCL-tests v2.17.1 is built and linkable against both the vanilla NCCL 2.23.4 and R²CCL libraries for microbenchmark runs on the two-node testbed.

verification.spec: Build nccl-tests at tag v2.17.1 twice — once linked against vanilla NCCL 2.23.4, once against R2CCL. Run `all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 1M -f 2 -g 8` on a single node with each build; both must run to completion without link errors.

sub_tasks.requirements: Megatron-LM is installed and configured on the testbed for running GPT-3 2.7B (DP=16) and 13B (TP=8, PP=2) training benchmarks used in Section 8.2.

verification.spec: Install Megatron-LM at the version compatible with PyTorch 2.10.0 + NCCL 2.23.4. Launch a short (2-3 iteration) smoke run of GPT-3 2.7B with DP=16 and a separate smoke run of GPT-3 13B with TP=8, PP=2 on the 2-node 16xH100 testbed. Verify both configurations reach a training step boundary and emit tokens/sec throughput.

sub_tasks.requirements: Baseline systems used for comparison are installed and runnable in the same environment.
AdapCC is installed as the training baseline and can be selected as the collective backend for Megatron-LM runs.

verification.spec: Install AdapCC per its published release (or reproduce via source). Confirm it can be selected as a Megatron-LM communication backend by launching a small Megatron-LM GPT training job (single node, tiny model, 10 iterations) with AdapCC as the collective library and verify iterations complete.

sub_tasks.requirements: DéjàVu is built both with its original NCCL backend and with NCCL replaced by R²CCL, and both builds can serve the OPT-66B and BLOOM-176B inference workloads described in Section 8.3.

verification.spec: Build DejaVu twice: once with its original NCCL backend, once with NCCL symlinked/replaced by R2CCL. For each build, launch OPT-66B inference with TP=8 PP=2 on the two-node testbed and confirm the engine can serve a single prompt to completion. Repeat sanity check with BLOOM-176B if memory allows (else confirm binary launches with parallel init).

sub_tasks.requirements: Restart Server and Reroute Request mitigation strategies are implemented as vLLM harness options; the Restart Server path enforces a fixed 35-second restart delay as measured in the paper.

verification.spec: Inspect the vLLM harness code for two baseline strategies: (1) Restart Server — trigger a simulated NIC failure and assert the harness records a delay of exactly 35.0s (±0.5s) before service resumes, measured via timestamps in the log. (2) Reroute Request — assert affected requests are redirected to the alternate server and the alternate absorbs 2x load (log shows request count doubled during failure window).

sub_tasks.requirements: The SimAI-based simulation environment for large-scale experiments is set up according to the paper's configuration.
SimAI (Wang et al., 2025) is installed and runnable end-to-end for producing training-time simulations used in Section 8.2.

verification.spec: Clone and build SimAI (Wang et al. 2025) per its README. Run the shipped example configured for NVIDIA Spectrum-X RoCE-v2 rail-optimized topology with 8xA100/8x200Gbps NICs per server across at least 4 servers, and confirm the simulator produces an end-to-end training-time report (iteration time, communication breakdown) without errors.

sub_tasks.requirements: SimAI is configured with NVIDIA's Spectrum-X RoCE-v2 rail-optimized topology as the network model.

verification.spec: Inspect the SimAI configuration files used for R2CCL experiments. Verify the network topology parameter is set to 'Spectrum-X' rail-optimized RoCE-v2 (or an equivalent labeled configuration file matching NVIDIA Spectrum-X topology parameters: rail-optimized layout, RoCE-v2 transport). Confirm via grep on config yaml/json or the topology generator invocation.

sub_tasks.requirements: Each simulated server in SimAI is provisioned with 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs and 8 200Gbps NICs, matching the paper's simulation setup.

verification.spec: Inspect the SimAI configuration used for R2CCL experiments and verify per-server parameters: exactly 8 GPUs of type A100 per server and exactly 8 NICs per server at 200 Gbps. Confirm by parsing the SimAI config file(s) and asserting these fields.

sub_tasks.requirements: The simulation harness supports cluster sizes ranging from 32 to 1024 GPUs, and can instantiate the specific configurations used (4–64 servers for 7B, 1024 GPUs for 175B, 64 GPUs for RLHF, 512 GPUs for multi-failure Monte Carlo).

verification.spec: Run the SimAI harness with cluster sizes {32, 512, 1024} GPUs and the specific configurations reported: (a) 7B model on 4-64 servers, (b) 175B with TP=8, PP=8, DP=16 on 1024 GPUs, (c) RLHF fine-tuning on 64 GPUs (TP=8, PP=1, DP=8), (d) 512-GPU multi-failure Monte Carlo. Verify each configuration launches and produces a completion-time output without configuration errors.

sub_tasks.requirements: Failure-injection tooling required to reproduce experiments is implemented and integrated with both the physical testbed and simulator.
A NIC failure-injection utility is implemented that can disable one or more specified InfiniBand NICs on a chosen node at a configurable timestamp (e.g., t=50s for inference experiments).

verification.spec: Invoke the NIC failure-injection utility with arguments (node_id, nic_id_list, failure_timestamp) and confirm that: (1) at the specified simulation/wallclock time t, the specified NIC(s) on the specified node become unreachable (verified via connectivity probe or ibstat / SimAI event log), (2) multiple NICs and multiple nodes can be targeted in one invocation, (3) failure timing is honored within ~100ms for the physical testbed and exactly at the specified step for simulation.

sub_tasks.requirements: The SimAI simulation harness supports injecting k concurrent NIC failures (k in 1..10) across a 64-server/512-GPU cluster with configurable spatial distribution for Monte Carlo runs.

verification.spec: Run the SimAI harness in a 64-server / 512-GPU configuration and invoke the multi-failure injection API with k in {1, 5, 10}. For each k, run at least 3 random seeds and verify: (1) exactly k NICs across the cluster are marked failed in the simulator's event log, (2) the spatial distribution (which servers host the failed NICs) is controllable via a seed/pattern parameter, (3) simulation completes and reports iteration times. Verify Monte Carlo aggregation over 50 patterns per k is supported.

sub_tasks.requirements: Bilateral failure awareness via OOB notification and three-point RDMA probe triangulation are implemented to detect and locate NIC/link failures.
Error interception at the NCCL InfiniBand transport layer prevents crash-on-error and surfaces failures to higher-level R2CCL logic.
Code has been implemented to hook into the NCCL InfiniBand plugin's Completion Queue (CQ) polling path so that CQE errors are captured rather than allowed to crash the process.

verification.spec: Grep the R2CCL patch to NCCL's InfiniBand plugin source (net_ib.cc or equivalent). Verify that the ibv_poll_cq / CQ polling loop is wrapped so that CQEs with status != IBV_WC_SUCCESS are captured and dispatched to the R2CCL failover handler rather than being propagated as a fatal error (i.e., no direct call to abort()/WARN+return ncclSystemError without invoking failover). Confirm the modified path exists in the diff against upstream NCCL 2.23.4.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to detect Queue Pair (QP) transition into error state and report the affected connection identifier to the R2CCL failover controller.

verification.spec: Grep the R2CCL IB plugin source for QP state monitoring: verify a code path queries QP state (ibv_query_qp) or catches transition to IBV_QPS_ERR, extracts the QP number / connection identifier, and calls a failover-controller function passing this identifier. Confirm the connection identifier maps back to a (rank, channel, NIC) tuple used elsewhere in R2CCL.

sub_tasks.requirements: When a network error is detected, the modified proxy send/receive progress loop reports the operation as a failed request instead of aborting, keeping the application process alive.

verification.spec: Launch a small NCCL AllReduce collective with R2CCL enabled. Inject a NIC failure mid-collective (via the failure-injection utility). Verify via process monitoring that: (1) the application process does NOT exit or crash for at least 30 seconds after the failure, (2) the proxy progress loop logs the failed request as 'failed' with the operation identifier, (3) subsequent collective calls can still be issued from the same process.

sub_tasks.requirements: Bilateral failure awareness broadcasts fault notifications over an out-of-band bootstrap network so both endpoints react to a failure without half-open waits.
Code has been implemented to establish an out-of-band (OOB) bootstrap network (e.g., MPI over TCP on a non-datapath NIC) separate from the RDMA data path, used for exchanging failure notifications.

verification.spec: Start an R2CCL communicator across 2 nodes and inspect: (1) that an MPI (or equivalent) bootstrap connection is initialized during ncclCommInitRank, (2) that this bootstrap uses a NIC/interface distinct from the data-path RDMA NICs (verify via configuration and netstat/lsof showing the OOB socket bound to a non-datapath interface), (3) that a test message can be sent over this OOB channel independent of the RDMA data path (e.g., inject data-path failure and confirm OOB still delivers).

sub_tasks.requirements: Upon local detection of a connection error, the endpoint immediately sends a failure-notification message to its peer over the OOB channel identifying the affected connection.

verification.spec: In a 2-node R2CCL setup, instrument the OOB send path with a logger. Inject a local RDMA connection error on node A. Verify: (1) node A calls the OOB send function within milliseconds of detecting the error, (2) the outgoing message payload contains a connection identifier that matches the failed connection (rank/channel/NIC tuple), (3) node B receives this message on its OOB listener.

sub_tasks.requirements: Upon receiving an OOB failure notification, the peer transitions the corresponding connection out of the polling/waiting state to avoid spinning on a dead connection.

verification.spec: On a 2-node R2CCL setup, cause node A to send an OOB failure notification identifying a specific connection. Instrument node B's connection state machine and verify: (1) upon receipt of the OOB notification, the corresponding connection's state transitions out of the polling/waiting state (e.g., to a 'failed' or 'migrating' state) within milliseconds, (2) node B's proxy thread no longer spins on that connection's CQ (verify via CPU profile or explicit state check).

sub_tasks.requirements: After fault localization, the final failure information (faulty endpoint / link classification) is broadcast to all ranks in the communicator via the OOB channel.

verification.spec: In a >=3-node R2CCL setup, trigger a failure and complete fault localization. Instrument each rank's OOB receive queue and verify that every rank in the communicator receives a broadcast message containing the finalized failure classification (faulty endpoint identifier and/or link classification). Confirm the broadcast completes within a bounded time (< 1s) after localization.

sub_tasks.requirements: End-to-end failure detection latency (from local error to peer acknowledgement of the OOB notification) is on the order of milliseconds rather than minutes, as claimed in Section 4.1.

verification.spec: Instrument R2CCL's bilateral failure awareness path: on a 2-node H100+InfiniBand testbed running a collective (e.g., AllReduce loop via NCCL-tests linked against R2CCL), inject a NIC failure on one endpoint (e.g., by disabling the IB port with `ibportstate ... disable` or unplugging via software). Timestamp (a) the moment the local endpoint's CQ/QP returns an error and (b) the moment the peer receives and processes the OOB notification over the bootstrap MPI/TCP channel. Report the delta averaged over >=10 injections. Success = median detection-to-peer-notification latency is on the order of milliseconds (<=100 ms with tolerance 0.9, i.e., <=~1 s), clearly not minutes.

sub_tasks.requirements: A dedicated probe QP pool isolated from data paths is provisioned at initialization to support fault-localization probing.
Code has been implemented to allocate a probe Queue Pair pool per NIC at communicator initialization, distinct from the QPs used for collective data traffic.

verification.spec: Grep the R2CCL source for a probe QP pool allocator invoked during ncclCommInitRank / communicator setup. Verify: (1) a distinct set of QPs is created per NIC labeled as 'probe' QPs, (2) these QPs are stored in a data structure separate from the data-path QP array, (3) the allocator is called before any collective operation begins.

sub_tasks.requirements: Probe QPs are excluded from the datapath schedulers so probing traffic does not interfere with or share completion queues with regular collective operations.

verification.spec: Inspect the R2CCL datapath scheduler and CQ handling code. Verify: (1) probe QPs are NOT added to the datapath QP list iterated by the collective progress loop, (2) probe QPs have their own dedicated CQ(s) distinct from the CQs used by collective data-path QPs (confirm via ibv_create_cq call sites and the CQ passed to ibv_create_qp for probe vs. data QPs).

sub_tasks.requirements: Three-point RDMA probe triangulation localizes the failure to a specific NIC or link by correlating outcomes from both endpoints and an auxiliary node.
Code has been implemented so that upon detecting a suspected failure, both endpoints and a selected auxiliary NIC (on a third node) each issue zero-byte RDMA Write probes to the suspected peers.

verification.spec: Set up a 3-node RDMA test (or a mocked RDMA verbs harness) with a controllable fault-injection layer. Trigger a simulated failure on a connection between nodes A and B. Verify via instrumentation/logging that: (1) node A issues a zero-byte RDMA Write probe to node B, (2) node B issues a zero-byte RDMA Write probe to node A, and (3) a designated auxiliary node C also issues zero-byte RDMA Write probes to A and/or B. Confirm the operations are RDMA Writes of size 0 (via captured verbs API calls or wire trace).

sub_tasks.requirements: The auxiliary node is selected from a cluster of >=3 nodes such that it uses a NIC distinct from the two suspected endpoints; in <3-node clusters the code falls back to endpoint-only diagnosis.

verification.spec: Run auxiliary-node selection logic under two scenarios: (a) 3+ node cluster: verify the selector returns a third node whose probing NIC is distinct from the two suspected endpoints' NICs (check node id != endpoint node ids AND NIC id differs); (b) 2-node cluster: verify the code path falls back to endpoint-only diagnosis (no auxiliary node used, distinct branch taken as confirmed via logging or code-coverage instrumentation).

sub_tasks.requirements: Probe outcomes are classified into (immediate local error) vs. (timeout / retry-exceeded) categories based on completion status returned by the probe QP.

verification.spec: Feed the probe-classification module with synthetic RDMA completion outcomes: (1) a completion with an immediate error status (e.g., IBV_WC_REM_ACCESS_ERR / IBV_WC_LOC_QP_OP_ERR) and (2) a completion representing timeout / retry-exceeded (IBV_WC_RETRY_EXC_ERR or no completion within timeout). Verify the classifier tags them as 'immediate_local_error' vs 'timeout_retry_exceeded' respectively.

sub_tasks.requirements: A decision rule identifies a NIC hardware failure when the local endpoint's probe produces immediate errors while its peer observes only timeouts.

verification.spec: Feed the triangulation decision function inputs corresponding to: local endpoint probe = immediate_local_error, peer endpoint probe = timeout, auxiliary probe to local endpoint = timeout. Verify the function returns classification 'local NIC hardware failure' identifying the local endpoint's NIC as faulty. Test with the mirror case (peer immediate, local timeout) and verify symmetry (peer NIC identified).

sub_tasks.requirements: A decision rule identifies a broken link when both endpoints observe timeouts on their probes, and uses the auxiliary NIC's probe results to distinguish single-endpoint from dual-endpoint impairment.

verification.spec: Feed the triangulation decision function inputs where both endpoints' probes report timeouts. Test two sub-cases: (a) auxiliary NIC probe to endpoint A succeeds while probe to endpoint B times out -> classifier returns 'link failure, single-endpoint impairment on B'; (b) auxiliary NIC probes to both endpoints time out -> classifier returns 'link failure, dual-endpoint impairment or broken shared link'. Verify both classifications are emitted correctly.

sub_tasks.requirements: The correlated triangulation result (faulty NIC identifier or link classification) is emitted as a structured record consumed by the OOB broadcast and the live-migration/failover-list module.

verification.spec: Inspect the triangulation module's output. Verify: (1) it produces a structured record (e.g., C struct or serializable object) with named fields such as {classification, faulty_nic_id, endpoint_ranks, link_id}, (2) this record is consumed by both the OOB broadcast function (grep for the record type in the OOB send path) and the live-migration / failover-list module (grep for its use in selecting backup NICs).

sub_tasks.requirements: Periodic re-probing detects component recovery so that repaired NICs/links can be reinstated into the failover pool.
Code has been implemented to periodically re-issue zero-byte RDMA probes against previously failed NICs/links to detect recovery events (e.g., NIC resets, cable fixes).

verification.spec: Simulate a NIC-failed state in the probe subsystem, then observe over a fixed interval (e.g., 5 seconds) that the code periodically issues zero-byte RDMA Write probes toward the failed endpoint. Verify via logging or mock RDMA interface that multiple probe attempts are dispatched, and that once probes succeed the NIC is marked recovered.

sub_tasks.requirements: The probe frequency and strategy are adapted based on observed failure and recovery history (e.g., backoff on persistent failures, faster probing on intermittent flapping) as described in Section 4.2.

verification.spec: Inject synthetic failure/recovery histories (persistent failure vs intermittent flapping) into the probe scheduler and verify that probe intervals adapt: persistent failures should trigger back-off (increasing intervals), intermittent flapping should trigger faster probing (shorter intervals). Assert measured probe timestamps match these regimes.

sub_tasks.requirements: Upon detecting recovery of a previously failed NIC/link, the component is marked healthy and re-inserted into the per-channel failover list ordered by PCIe distance.

verification.spec: Mark a NIC as failed in the health-status table, then simulate a successful recovery probe. Inspect the per-channel failover list and verify (a) the NIC is flagged healthy, and (b) it is re-inserted at the position dictated by PCIe distance to the source GPU (i.e., ordering invariant preserved).

sub_tasks.requirements: Multi-NIC GPU buffer registration and DMA-buffer rollback enable lossless in-flight connection migration to backup NICs.
GPU-NIC multi-registration proactively registers each GPU buffer with all NICs at communicator initialization so any backup NIC can access buffers without on-demand re-registration.
Multi-NIC registration structural implementation exists.

Code has been implemented that hooks NCCL's memory-registration path in the ncclNet plugin layer to iterate over all NICs on a server and register each GPU buffer with every NIC during communicator initialization.

verification.spec: Inspect the modified ncclNet plugin source and confirm the memory-registration path iterates over all NICs discovered on the node and registers each GPU buffer with every NIC during ncclCommInitRank. Run a small init test on the H100 testbed and confirm via logging that every GPU buffer has N registration handles where N is the number of NICs.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that extends the connection-setup logic to create additional RDMA queue pairs on each backup NIC in parallel with the primary connection so that backup connections exist at bootstrap.

verification.spec: Run communicator initialization on the two-node testbed and, via ibv/QP inspection or logging, verify that for each channel additional RDMA QPs are created on every backup NIC (not only the primary) at bootstrap time.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that stores the resulting NIC/QP handles in a per-channel failover list attached to each communicator channel.

verification.spec: Inspect the communicator/channel data structure and verify each channel has a failover list field populated with the set of (NIC, QP) handles for that channel. Confirm via test that the list length equals the number of NICs per node.

sub_tasks.requirements: Backup NIC ordering by PCIe distance is implemented.

Code has been implemented that computes PCIe distance between each source GPU and every NIC on the server (using NCCL topology info) and sorts each channel's failover list in ascending PCIe-distance order.

verification.spec: Using NCCL's topology info (nvmlDeviceGetPciInfo or existing NCCL topo graph), verify the per-channel failover list is sorted by PCIe distance ascending relative to the source GPU. Test by constructing a mock topology with known distances and asserting the sorted order.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that during migration the system iterates over the ordered failover list and selects the first NIC whose health status is healthy as the active backup, supporting successive failovers by advancing to the next entry.

verification.spec: Mark the first entry in a channel's failover list as failed and trigger migration; verify the second entry is selected. Then mark the second as failed and verify the third is selected (successive failover). Assert the selection function returns the first healthy entry each time.

sub_tasks.requirements: Registration is performed only at initialization (not on the recovery path) and installs mapping entries without duplicating buffer contents, keeping migration latency in the low-millisecond range.

verification.spec: On a 2-node H100+InfiniBand testbed with R2CCL integrated into NCCL, verify two properties: (1) Multi-NIC GPU buffer registration occurs only during ncclCommInitRank/bootstrap — instrument the ncclNet plugin to log ibv_reg_mr calls and confirm no registration calls occur on the failover/recovery path when a NIC failure is injected mid-collective. (2) Measure end-to-end live-migration latency: from OOB failure notification to first retransmitted chunk completing on the backup NIC, over >=10 injected NIC failures during an AllReduce. Report median. Success = (a) zero ibv_reg_mr calls on recovery path AND (b) median migration latency in the low-millisecond range (paper_value 10 ms, tolerance 0.9 => <=~100 ms accepted).

sub_tasks.requirements: For GPU-NIC pairs lacking direct GPUDirect access or crossing NUMA, code has been implemented that binds the collective to pinned host buffers and uses CPU-assisted copies so GPU memory footprint remains unchanged.

verification.spec: Configure a GPU-NIC pair without GPUDirect (or spanning NUMA) and trigger a collective. Verify via code inspection and runtime tracing that the transport uses pinned host buffers with CPU-assisted copies, and that GPU memory footprint (measured via cudaMemGetInfo before/after registration) is unchanged.

sub_tasks.requirements: End-to-end live-migration behavior maintains correctness and low latency during mid-collective NIC failures.

Behavioral test: injecting a NIC failure mid-collective (e.g., mid-AllReduce chunk transfer) causes the collective to complete with bit-identical results to a no-failure run on the same inputs, demonstrating lossless in-flight migration.

verification.spec: Run an AllReduce over 2 nodes x 8 H100 GPUs on a deterministic input tensor (e.g., filled with rank id, float32, 256MB). Record the resulting reduced tensor. Repeat the run with R2CCL enabled and mid-collective inject a NIC failure by disabling one CX-7 port via `ip link set <ib_iface> down` after a random delay during the collective. Assert the returned tensor is bitwise identical (torch.equal) to the no-failure result across 10 trials.

sub_tasks.requirements: Behavioral test: after a NIC failure, the communicator is not re-initialized (no ncclCommInitRank re-invocation) and the application process does not restart, confirmed by logging/tracing hooks.

verification.spec: Instrument ncclCommInitRank with a call counter and monitor process PID. Run a PyTorch job on 2 nodes, inject a NIC failure mid-training, and verify (a) ncclCommInitRank counter does not increment post-init, (b) the PID of the training process remains unchanged across the failure event.

sub_tasks.requirements: Behavioral test: successive NIC failures on the same channel are handled by advancing through the ordered failover list without job termination, as long as at least one healthy inter-node path remains.

verification.spec: On a 2-node H100 testbed with 8 NICs/node, fail NICs one at a time on the same channel (up to N-1 NICs) during a running collective. Verify the job continues without termination as long as at least one healthy path remains, and that job termination only occurs when all NICs on the channel fail.

sub_tasks.requirements: Measured: end-to-end migration latency (from OOB failure notification to first chunk successfully retransmitted on backup NIC) is in the low-millisecond range on the two-node H100 testbed.

verification.spec: Instrument the OOB notification handler and the backup-NIC send path with high-resolution timestamps. Trigger a NIC failure during an AllReduce on the 2-node H100 testbed and measure the elapsed time from OOB notification receipt to first successful CQE on the backup NIC. Report median over 20 trials.

sub_tasks.requirements: Measured: with hot-repair only (single-NIC bottleneck on the affected node after migration), NCCL-tests AllReduce bus-bandwidth throughput on large messages drops by approximately 46% relative to the no-failure vanilla NCCL baseline, matching the reported single-NIC-bottleneck loss.

verification.spec: Run NCCL-tests `all_reduce_perf -b 512M -e 16G -f 2 -g 8` on 2 nodes with vanilla NCCL (no failure) to establish baseline bus bandwidth for large messages. Then run the same with R2CCL in hot-repair-only mode (disable Balance and R2CCL-AllReduce) with one CX-7 NIC administratively disabled at start. Compute percent throughput loss = 100*(1 - bw_hotrepair/bw_baseline) averaged over messages >=512MB. Assert value ~46%.

sub_tasks.requirements: Measured: with hot-repair only, NCCL-tests AllGather, ReduceScatter, and SendRecv throughput on large messages exhibits approximately 50% loss relative to the no-failure baseline, consistent with the reported single-NIC bottleneck.

verification.spec: Run nccl-tests v2.17.1 for AllGather, ReduceScatter, and SendRecv on the 2-node H100 testbed with 1 NIC failed and R2CCL configured in hot-repair-only mode (Balance disabled). At large message sizes (>=512 MB), measure bus bandwidth and compare against the no-failure baseline; the loss should be ~50%.

sub_tasks.requirements: PXN- and NUMA-aware load redistribution across remaining healthy NICs is implemented as a drop-in balancer for all collectives except throughput-oriented AllReduce.

R²CCL-Balance is integrated into NCCL's enqueue/planning path so that it intercepts collective invocations before ring/tree instantiation and consults per-NIC health status to redistribute affected channels.

Code has been implemented that hooks into NCCL's enqueue and planning logic (ncclEnqueue / ncclLaunchKernel path) to invoke R²CCL-Balance prior to algorithm selection and ring/tree construction, so channel-to-NIC assignments can be modified.

verification.spec: Grep the R2CCL patch/source for hooks into NCCL's enqueue planning path (e.g., ncclEnqueueCheck, getAlgoInfo, ncclTopoCompute*, or the algorithm/protocol selection functions in enqueue.cc). Verify that (a) a callback or code insertion invokes R2CCL-Balance BEFORE the algorithm/protocol is finalized and BEFORE ring/tree construction, and (b) the invocation has access to per-NIC health status such that channel-to-NIC assignments can be modified in-place before kernel launch.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that maintains per-node/per-NIC health status records (e.g., failed/healthy flags updated by the failure-detection subsystem) and exposes them to the R²CCL-Balance planner at collective enqueue time.

verification.spec: Inspect the R2CCL codebase for a per-node/per-NIC health status table (e.g., array of enum {HEALTHY, FAILED}). Verify the failure-detection subsystem writes to it and the Balance planner reads from it at ncclEnqueue time. Confirm via a unit test that toggling status affects planner decisions.

sub_tasks.requirements: R²CCL-Balance leaves the underlying NCCL collective algorithm (ring/tree/hierarchical) unchanged, intervening only at the network/transport layer to reassign channels; the collective algorithm selection logic itself is not altered by Balance.

verification.spec: Diff R2CCL against NCCL 2.23.4 in the algorithm-selection module (ring/tree/hierarchical decision). Verify Balance does not modify the algorithm chosen; it only reassigns channels at the network layer. Confirm via a test that with Balance enabled, the same collective algorithm (e.g., ring) is selected as without Balance.

sub_tasks.requirements: R²CCL-Balance redistributes the traffic that would have used a failed NIC across the remaining healthy NICs on the affected server proportionally to their available bandwidth headroom.

Code has been implemented that, given per-server data volume D_i determined by the NCCL schedule and a set of failed NICs on server i, computes a redistribution of the failed-NIC share across surviving NICs weighted by their remaining available bandwidth.

verification.spec: Provide the Balance planner a synthetic input: D_i = 1 GB, 8 NICs of equal bandwidth on server i with 1 failed. Verify that the failed NIC's 1/8 share is redistributed as 1/7 additional load to each of the 7 healthy NICs (proportional to their bandwidth). Test with heterogeneous bandwidths (e.g., one NIC at half speed) and assert the redistribution is weighted accordingly.

sub_tasks.requirements: The balancer preserves each server's cross-server data volume D_i (i.e., it does not attempt to shrink D_i, only redistributes the fraction that was assigned to the failed NIC), consistent with the paper's overhead analysis stating ReduceScatter/AllGather/Broadcast volumes cannot be reduced by rescheduling.

verification.spec: For each supported collective (ReduceScatter, AllGather, Broadcast) run with and without Balance under a NIC failure, and verify total inter-server bytes sent per server i (measured via NIC counters) equals the pre-failure D_i determined by the NCCL schedule. Balance must not decrease D_i, only redistribute across surviving NICs.

sub_tasks.requirements: For each rerouted flow, Balance selects a specific backup NIC per channel; the mapping is deterministic given (failed NIC set, PCIe/NUMA topology, NVLink availability).

verification.spec: Instantiate the Balance NIC selection function twice with identical (failed NIC set, PCIe/NUMA topology, NVLink availability) inputs and verify the per-channel backup-NIC mapping is bit-identical. Then vary one input at a time and verify the mapping changes deterministically.

sub_tasks.requirements: The topology-aware per-flow forwarding policy chooses between direct PCIe forwarding and NVLink PXN proxy forwarding based on NUMA locality and available headroom.

Code has been implemented that parses PCIe/NUMA topology (e.g., via hwloc or NCCL's topology graph) to determine, for every (source GPU, target NIC) pair, whether they share a NUMA node and their PCIe distance.

verification.spec: Import the topology parsing module and confirm it exposes a function that, given (source GPU id, target NIC id), returns (same_numa: bool, pcie_distance: int). Feed synthetic hwloc/NCCL topology fixtures and check returned values match expected NUMA/PCIe distance.

sub_tasks.requirements: When the source GPU and the backup target NIC lie on the same NUMA node and the direct PCIe path has sufficient bandwidth headroom, R²CCL-Balance selects direct PCIe forwarding (prioritized over PXN).

verification.spec: Construct a synthetic topology where source GPU and backup NIC share NUMA and the direct PCIe path has headroom > threshold. Invoke Balance's path selector and assert it returns 'direct_pcie' (not PXN).

sub_tasks.requirements: When the backup NIC lies on a different NUMA node, the planner compares the cost of PCIe + CPU-interconnect (QPI/UPI) forwarding against NVLink PXN forwarding via a proxy GPU co-located with the target NIC, and selects the lower-cost path.

verification.spec: Construct a synthetic topology with cross-NUMA backup NIC. Set (a) PCIe+QPI cost lower than PXN and confirm selector returns PCIe+CPU-interconnect; (b) PXN cost lower and confirm selector returns PXN via proxy GPU co-located with target NIC.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that accounts for the extra PCIe-lane headroom freed by a failed NIC (the affinity GPU no longer drives the failed NIC) when computing PCIe path costs for detoured flows.

verification.spec: In the PCIe cost function, verify that marking a NIC as failed increases the available PCIe headroom on the affinity GPU's PCIe lane (compared to same topology with NIC healthy but idle). Confirm this freed headroom is used when scoring detoured flows.

sub_tasks.requirements: Given a controlled failure of a single NIC where the affinity GPU shares NUMA with another surviving NIC on the same server, the Balance policy selects direct PCIe forwarding (not PXN) for that GPU's rerouted traffic.

verification.spec: On 2x8xH100 testbed (or simulated equivalent), fail one NIC whose affinity GPU shares NUMA with a surviving NIC. Run an AllGather and inspect Balance's traffic routing log; assert rerouted flow uses direct PCIe to the same-NUMA NIC, not PXN via NVLink.

sub_tasks.requirements: Given a controlled failure where the only surviving NICs are on a different NUMA node and NVLink PXN offers lower cost than cross-socket PCIe, the Balance policy selects PXN forwarding via a proxy GPU.

verification.spec: In simulator or on testbed, fail all NICs on the affinity NUMA node so surviving NICs are on the remote NUMA. Configure NVLink PXN cost lower than cross-socket PCIe. Trigger Balance and confirm rerouted flow uses PXN through a proxy GPU co-located with the target NIC.

sub_tasks.requirements: R²CCL-Balance is applied to all collectives listed in Table 1 (ReduceScatter, AllGather, Broadcast, Reduce, P2P Send/Recv and All-to-All, and latency-bound AllReduce) but not to throughput-oriented AllReduce, which uses R²CCL-AllReduce.
Code has been implemented so that ReduceScatter, AllGather, Broadcast, Reduce, and P2P (Send/Recv, All-to-All) collective invocations under NIC failure are dispatched through the R²CCL-Balance path.

verification.spec: For each collective in {ReduceScatter, AllGather, Broadcast, Reduce, Send/Recv, All-to-All}, inject a NIC failure and confirm via logging or hook instrumentation that the R²CCL-Balance code path is entered (rather than HotRepair-only or crash).

sub_tasks.requirements: For AllReduce, the runtime selects between R²CCL-Balance (latency-bound / small messages) and R²CCL-AllReduce (throughput-oriented / large messages) based on the α–β performance model using message size and per-link α, β parameters supplied by NCCL.

verification.spec: Call the AllReduce dispatcher with a range of message sizes (8B, 1MB, 32MB, 512MB, 4GB) under a simulated NIC failure. Verify small sizes select Balance and large sizes select R²CCL-AllReduce, with the crossover consistent with the α–β model evaluated on supplied per-link parameters.

sub_tasks.requirements: R²CCL-Balance's measured behavior on the two-node H100 testbed matches the paper's reported throughput preservation ratios versus the no-failure NCCL baseline.

On the two-node 8×H100 / 8×CX-7 400G IB testbed with a single injected NIC failure, R²CCL-Balance sustains approximately 92% of the no-failure NCCL AllReduce bus bandwidth for small messages (<32 MB).

verification.spec: Run NCCL-tests `all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 32M -f 2 -g 8` on 2 nodes with vanilla NCCL (no failure) to establish per-size baseline bus BW. Then run identical config with R2CCL-Balance and one CX-7 NIC disabled. For each message size <32MB, compute ratio bw_balance/bw_baseline; assert median ratio ~0.92.

sub_tasks.requirements: On the same testbed, R²CCL-Balance sustains approximately 83% of the no-failure NCCL AllReduce bus bandwidth for large messages (≥512 MB), and 87–98% for medium messages (32–256 MB).

verification.spec: Run NCCL-tests `all_reduce_perf -b 32M -e 4G -f 2 -g 8` on 2 nodes with vanilla NCCL (no failure) and with R2CCL-Balance under one NIC failure. Bucket results into medium (32MB–256MB) and large (>=512MB); compute bw_balance/bw_baseline in each bucket. Assert median large-bucket ratio ~0.83 and medium-bucket ratios within 0.87–0.98.

sub_tasks.requirements: On the same testbed, R²CCL-Balance sustains 85–89% of the no-failure NCCL bus bandwidth for AllGather, ReduceScatter, and SendRecv for large messages under a single NIC failure (Figure 16 / Appendix E).

verification.spec: Using NCCL-tests, run `all_gather_perf`, `reduce_scatter_perf`, and `sendrecv_perf` at large message sizes (>=512MB) on 2 nodes x 8 H100, once with vanilla NCCL (no failure) and once with R2CCL-Balance under one NIC failure. Compute bw_balance/bw_baseline for each op at each large size. Assert per-op ratios fall within 85%–89% (target ~87%).

sub_tasks.requirements: R²CCL-HotRepair (no balancing) on the same testbed under a single NIC failure yields approximately 50% (≈46%) throughput loss for large-message AllReduce and ~50% for AllGather/ReduceScatter/SendRecv, confirming the baseline degradation that Balance is measured against.

verification.spec: Run NCCL-tests AllReduce, AllGather, ReduceScatter, and SendRecv at large message sizes (>=512MB) on 2 nodes x 8 H100 with one NIC failed and only R²CCL-HotRepair (no balance/allreduce optimization) enabled. Measure bus bandwidth relative to no-failure baseline and confirm ~50% throughput loss (46-54%).

sub_tasks.requirements: The two-stage partial+global AllReduce with tailored broadcast is implemented and correctly partitions data via the derived optimal Y* threshold on lost bandwidth X.
The R²CCL-AllReduce algorithm structure decomposes AllReduce into concurrent global+partial AllReduce first stage and tailored broadcast second stage.

Code has been implemented that partitions NCCL channels into two groups: one group executing a global AllReduce across all n servers (including the degraded server), and one group executing a partial AllReduce that excludes the degraded server.

verification.spec: Grep the R2CCL source for the AllReduce planner (e.g., R2CCLAllReducePlanner or channel-partition code) and confirm it splits NCCL channels into two disjoint groups: (a) a global AllReduce over all n ranks (rank list includes degraded server) and (b) a partial AllReduce excluding the degraded server (its ranks are omitted). Additionally run with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO on a 2-node run with a NIC failure and confirm the log shows two concurrent AllReduce channel groups with distinct rank sets.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the global AllReduce channel group and the partial AllReduce channel group execute concurrently in the first stage to saturate available bandwidth.

verification.spec: Instrument the R²CCL-AllReduce launch path to record kernel/channel start times for the global-AllReduce channel group and partial-AllReduce channel group. Confirm the two groups' active windows overlap for the majority of stage-1 duration (>=80% overlap).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for the tailored broadcast second stage comprising: a broadcast from the failure server node, a pipelined ring broadcast across healthy servers, and final delivery of the partial-AllReduce result from the last healthy node back to the failure node.

verification.spec: Inspect the R2CCL-AllReduce implementation (custom CUDA broadcast kernel + host scheduling code). Verify presence of three sub-components in the second stage: (a) a broadcast originating from the failure/degraded server node, (b) a pipelined ring broadcast across the healthy servers, and (c) a final delivery step that sends the partial-AllReduce result from the last healthy ring node back to the failure node. Use importlib/ast/grep on the R2CCL source tree to confirm functions or kernel launches implementing each sub-step exist and are wired together in the AllReduce planner.

sub_tasks.requirements: A custom CUDA broadcast kernel is implemented to disseminate the Partial AllReduce result to the degraded node in the second phase.

verification.spec: Locate the custom CUDA broadcast kernel source (a .cu file with __global__ kernel used only in R²CCL-AllReduce stage 2). Verify it is compiled into the R²CCL library, callable from the stage-2 dispatcher, and invoked on a small end-to-end test producing correct broadcast results at the degraded node.

sub_tasks.requirements: The algorithm guarantees semantic correctness: at completion, every server (including the degraded one) obtains the full correct AllReduce reduction result over all inputs.

verification.spec: Run R2CCL-AllReduce on a small multi-rank setup (e.g., 4 simulated ranks with one designated as the degraded/failure node with reduced bandwidth). Provide each rank with a distinct input tensor of known values. After the AllReduce completes, verify that every rank (including the degraded one) holds a buffer bitwise-equal (or within floating-point tolerance for sum reduction) to the reference AllReduce result computed by a trusted baseline (e.g., torch.distributed.all_reduce over NCCL without failure). Test across multiple tensor sizes and reduction ops (sum, max).

sub_tasks.requirements: The data-partition ratio Y* between global and partial AllReduce is derived from the α-β performance model and optimally minimizes total completion time.

Code implements the first-stage global AllReduce completion time model T1(Y) = 2(ng-1)/(ng) × (1-Y)D / ((1-X)B), where n is number of servers, g is GPUs per server, X is fractional bandwidth loss on the failure node, and B is healthy-node bandwidth.

verification.spec: Import the T1 function from the R²CCL performance model, evaluate at several (n, g, X, Y, D, B) tuples, and compare against the closed-form 2(ng-1)/(ng) * (1-Y)*D / ((1-X)*B). Assert relative error < 1e-6.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements the partial AllReduce completion time model T2(Y) = 2((n-1)g-1)/((n-1)g) × YD/(XB) over n-1 healthy servers.

verification.spec: Import T2 and evaluate at several parameter tuples; compare against 2((n-1)g-1)/((n-1)g) * Y*D/(X*B). Assert relative error < 1e-6.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements the second-stage broadcast time model T3(Y) = YD/(XB) using the remaining bandwidth of the failure node.

verification.spec: Import T3 and evaluate at several parameter tuples; compare against Y*D/(X*B). Assert relative error < 1e-6.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code computes the total completion time T(Y) = max(T1(Y), T2(Y)) + T3(Y) as the piecewise objective per Appendix A.

verification.spec: Import the total-time function T(Y); for several (n,g,X,D,B) settings and Y in {0.1,0.3,0.5,0.7,0.9}, confirm T(Y) equals max(T1(Y),T2(Y)) + T3(Y).

sub_tasks.requirements: The implementation numerically or analytically solves T1(Y*) = T2(Y*), producing the unique crossover Y* in (0,1) as derived in Appendix A.

verification.spec: Import the strategy-planner module. For representative (n,g,X,B,D) tuples (e.g., n=2,g=8,X=0.5,B=1,D=1), invoke the solver that computes Y* satisfying T1(Y)=T2(Y). Independently compute T1(Y*), T2(Y*) using the closed-form expressions in Section 5.2 and Appendix A, and assert |T1(Y*)-T2(Y*)| < 1e-6, and 0 < Y* < 1.

sub_tasks.requirements: The strategy selector uses the threshold X = ng/(3ng-2): for X in (0, 1/3] it selects standard ring AllReduce (Y=0 optimum), and for X in [1/3, 1) it selects R²CCL-AllReduce with Y=Y*.

verification.spec: Import the strategy-selector function that takes (n,g,X) and returns an enum in {STANDARD_RING, R2CCL_ALLREDUCE, Y_value}. Sweep X in [0.01, 0.99] step 0.01 for (n=2,g=8) and (n=8,g=8). Assert: for X <= 1/3 the selector returns STANDARD_RING (Y=0); for X > 1/3 it returns R2CCL_ALLREDUCE with Y=Y*. Also assert the internal threshold value equals ng/(3ng-2) for the given (n,g).

sub_tasks.requirements: Unit test: for representative (n, g) e.g., n=2, g=8 and a chosen X in (1/3, 1), the computed Y* matches the closed-form expression from Appendix A within numerical tolerance.

verification.spec: Unit test with n=2, g=8, X=0.5: compute Y* via the implementation and via the derived closed-form from Appendix A. Assert |Y*_impl - Y*_closed_form| < 1e-6. Repeat for X=0.75 and X=0.4 with the same (n,g). All three cases must pass.

sub_tasks.requirements: Unit test: monotonicity properties hold in code — T1(Y) is strictly decreasing and T2(Y) is strictly increasing in Y over [0,1], with T1(0)>T2(0) and T1(1)<T2(1).

verification.spec: For n=8, g=8, X=0.5, D=1e9, B=1e9, sample T1(Y) and T2(Y) at Y = 0.01..0.99 in 0.01 steps. Assert T1 strictly decreasing, T2 strictly increasing, T1(0)>T2(0), and T1(1)<T2(1).

sub_tasks.requirements: R²CCL-AllReduce integrates with NCCL's channel abstraction, α-β performance model, and runtime strategy planner.

The runtime uses NCCL's machine-specific α (per-link latency) and β (per-link bandwidth) parameters combined with operation data size D to dynamically choose between standard Ring AllReduce, R²CCL-Balance, and R²CCL-AllReduce.

verification.spec: Invoke the algorithm selector with mock α, β values and varying D covering the small/medium/large message regimes. Assert selector returns 'Ring' for small D (Balance-only regime), 'Balance' for medium, and 'R2CCL-AllReduce' for large D under failure, consistent with α–β model predictions.

sub_tasks.requirements: The R²CCL-AllReduce schedule is exposed on NCCL channels such that both AllReduce groups (global and partial) reuse pre-registered multi-NIC GPU buffers and existing channel infrastructure without communicator re-initialization.

verification.spec: Launch R²CCL-AllReduce and inspect the NCCL communicator: verify no ncclCommInitRank re-initialization occurs (init counter unchanged), verify both global and partial groups use pre-existing channels, and confirm GPU buffers are pre-registered with multiple NICs (registration count > 1 per buffer).

sub_tasks.requirements: Measured microbenchmark outcomes for R²CCL-AllReduce on the two-node H100 testbed match reported values from Section 8.4 / Figure 15.
Under a single NIC failure, R²CCL-HotRepair (no scheduling optimization) exhibits approximately 46% AllReduce bus-bandwidth loss for large messages relative to the no-failure vanilla NCCL baseline.

verification.spec: Same as leaf 71edaecb: run large-message (>=512MB) AllReduce with R2CCL configured to hot-repair-only (Balance and R2CCL-AllReduce disabled) after disabling one CX-7 NIC; compare against no-failure vanilla NCCL baseline. Assert percent loss ~46%.

sub_tasks.requirements: For small AllReduce messages (<32 MB) under a single NIC failure, R²CCL-Balance achieves ~92% of no-failure throughput while R²CCL-AllReduce achieves ~66%, confirming the coordination-overhead crossover.

verification.spec: Run NCCL-tests all_reduce_perf on message sizes <32MB, 2 nodes, one NIC failure injected. Under R2CCL-Balance vs R2CCL-AllReduce (forced), compare each to no-failure baseline. Assert Balance ratio ~0.92 and R2CCL-AllReduce ratio ~0.66. Report the R2CCL-AllReduce ratio for the tolerance check.

sub_tasks.requirements: For medium AllReduce messages (32 MB – 256 MB) under a single NIC failure, both R²CCL-Balance and R²CCL-AllReduce reach 87–98% of no-failure throughput.

verification.spec: Run NCCL-tests AllReduce on 2x8 H100 with one NIC failed, sweeping message sizes 32MB, 64MB, 128MB, 256MB under both R²CCL-Balance and R²CCL-AllReduce. Compute bus-bandwidth ratio vs no-failure baseline; assert every point falls in [0.87, 0.98].

sub_tasks.requirements: For large AllReduce messages (≥512 MB) under a single NIC failure, R²CCL-AllReduce achieves ~93% of no-failure throughput, outperforming R²CCL-Balance at ~83%.

verification.spec: Run NCCL-tests all_reduce_perf for messages >=512MB on 2 nodes with one NIC failure. Measure bw under R2CCL-AllReduce (forced) and under R2CCL-Balance (forced), each vs no-failure baseline. Assert R2CCL-AllReduce ratio ~0.93 and Balance ratio ~0.83; use R2CCL-AllReduce ratio for the tolerance check.

sub_tasks.requirements: R²CCL-AllReduce reduces the peak per-server AllReduce workload on the bottleneck server from 2D (standard ring) toward 1.75D under the reported single-failure bandwidth-loss configuration, matching the Figure 5 claim.

verification.spec: For the failure configuration in Figure 5 (one NIC failed of 8, i.e. X=0.125 net bandwidth loss on the affected server), instrument R²CCL-AllReduce to log per-server sent+received bytes for a total data size D. Compute peak-server data volume and confirm it is approximately 1.75D (vs 2D for standard ring).

sub_tasks.requirements: Topology-aware logical re-ranking with bridge nodes and recursive R²CCL-AllReduce decomposition are implemented to handle concurrent failures.
Topology-aware logical re-ranking (Algorithm 1) inserts bridge nodes to resolve rail mismatches between adjacent nodes with disjoint NIC failures.
Code has been implemented that represents each node's surviving rail set S_n and computes pairwise rail intersections |S_u ∩ S_v| for adjacent nodes in the logical ring.

verification.spec: Instantiate the ring re-ranking module with a synthetic ring of 4 nodes each carrying a rail set (e.g., {0,1,2,3} minus a random NIC per node). Verify the module returns |S_u ∩ S_v| for every adjacent pair matching Python set-intersection ground truth.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes the global bandwidth threshold B_global = min over nodes n in R of |S_n| and uses it to detect deficient adjacent pairs whose rail overlap falls below this threshold.

verification.spec: For a synthetic ring with heterogeneous rail-set sizes, invoke the module and assert B_global equals min_n |S_n|. Then verify all adjacent pairs (u,v) with |S_u ∩ S_v| < B_global are flagged as deficient and no others are flagged.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that collects all deficient adjacent (u,v) pairs into a candidate list and sorts them by severity (rail-gap size) in descending order before processing.

verification.spec: Construct a ring with multiple deficient pairs having distinct rail gaps. Invoke re-ranking and inspect the internal Candidates list; assert it contains exactly those deficient pairs and is sorted by (B_global - |S_u ∩ S_v|) descending.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, for each deficient pair (u,v), searches remaining nodes w for a bridge candidate and computes NewCap = min(|S_u ∩ S_w|, |S_w ∩ S_v|) as well as RemovalCap = |S_x ∩ S_y| where x,y are w's current neighbors.

verification.spec: For a deficient pair (u,v) in a synthetic ring, invoke bridge search and inspect logged NewCap and RemovalCap values for each candidate w. Assert NewCap = min(|S_u ∩ S_w|, |S_w ∩ S_v|) and RemovalCap = |S_x ∩ S_y| where x,y are w's neighbors, matching independent Python computation.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that accepts a bridge node w only when both NewCap ≥ B_global and RemovalCap ≥ B_global hold, ensuring the relocation does not create a new deficient edge.

verification.spec: Unit-test the bridge-acceptance predicate in Algorithm 1 lines 14-19: construct a synthetic ring with rail sets S_n such that a candidate bridge w has NewCap = min(|S_u ∩ S_w|, |S_w ∩ S_v|) >= B_global but RemovalCap = |S_x ∩ S_y| < B_global, and verify w is rejected. Then construct a case where both conditions hold and verify w is accepted. Also verify the case where NewCap < B_global is rejected regardless of RemovalCap.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that relocates the accepted bridge node between u and v in the ring R', modifying only the affected edges rather than rebuilding the entire ring.

verification.spec: Given a ring R' = [n0, n1, ..., nk] and an accepted bridge node w located elsewhere in R', call the relocation routine with edge (u=n_i, v=n_{i+1}) and verify: (1) w now appears between u and v in the output ring; (2) w's previous neighbors x, y are now adjacent; (3) all other node adjacencies are unchanged; (4) ring length is preserved.

sub_tasks.requirements: The re-ranking is a targeted repair that preserves most pre-existing RDMA connections: on a test topology with a single rail-mismatched pair, the number of ring edges changed by the algorithm is at most 3 (u-v edge plus the two edges around the relocated bridge).

verification.spec: Build a synthetic ring of >=6 nodes where exactly one adjacent pair (u,v) has |S_u ∩ S_v| < B_global and a valid bridge exists elsewhere. Run the re-ranking algorithm and compute the symmetric difference of edge sets between input ring R and output ring R'. Assert |edges_changed| <= 3.

sub_tasks.requirements: For a canonical two-neighbor rail-mismatch test (node u loses rail r, node v loses rail r'), the re-ranking algorithm produces a ring in which every adjacent pair has |S_a ∩ S_b| ≥ B_global whenever such a bridge exists.

verification.spec: Construct a canonical rail-mismatch scenario: 4+ nodes each with rail sets of size |S|, where u loses rail r (S_u = full \ {r}) and neighbor v loses a different rail r' (S_v = full \ {r'}), and at least one other node w has broader rail connectivity such that min(|S_u ∩ S_w|, |S_w ∩ S_v|) >= B_global. Run the re-ranking; for every adjacent pair (a,b) in the output ring, assert |S_a ∩ S_b| >= B_global.

sub_tasks.requirements: Recursive R²CCL-AllReduce decomposition handles a bandwidth spectrum by recursively peeling off sub-rings of successively faster nodes.
Code has been implemented that ranks all participating servers by their post-failure aggregate inter-node bandwidth to identify the slowest node at each recursion level.

verification.spec: Given a list of servers each with an inter-node aggregate bandwidth value (post-failure), call the ranking routine used by recursive R²CCL-AllReduce and assert it returns servers sorted (ascending or with identifiable slowest node); verify the identified slowest-at-current-level matches min-bandwidth for several test inputs including ties.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that forms an outer global ring including all servers whose data-chunk size is scaled to the slowest node's bandwidth.

verification.spec: Instantiate recursive AllReduce planning on a heterogeneous cluster spec (e.g., N=6 servers with bandwidths [100,100,100,50,80,80] Gbps). Verify the planner produces an outer global ring containing all N servers, and that the data chunk assigned to this ring is scaled to the slowest node's bandwidth (chunk_size proportional to min_bw / sum-of-bws or a documented equivalent), matching the algorithm description.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that isolates the slowest node and constructs a faster sub-ring from the remaining participants, and recurses further whenever residual bandwidth variance remains above a configured threshold.

verification.spec: Given a cluster with 3+ bandwidth tiers, invoke the recursive planner and assert: (1) after building the outer ring, the slowest node is excluded from the next sub-ring; (2) a sub-ring is formed over remaining nodes; (3) recursion continues while max-min bandwidth variance exceeds the configured threshold, and stops otherwise. Provide inputs that trigger 1, 2, and 3 recursion levels and verify depth matches expectations.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that assigns each recursive sub-ring a data-chunk share proportional to the incremental bandwidth of its members, so faster subsets carry proportionally more data.

verification.spec: For a cluster with per-node bandwidths [B1<=B2<=...<=Bn], run the planner and assert that the data-chunk size assigned to each sub-ring is proportional to the incremental bandwidth (B_{i+1}-B_i) * (number of members in that sub-ring), so that sum of chunks equals the total AllReduce data D. Test on at least two configurations.

sub_tasks.requirements: The topology-aware logical re-ranking (Algorithm 1) is invoked at every level of the recursion to repair rail mismatches introduced by skipping slower nodes in inner sub-rings.

verification.spec: Instrument (or spy on) the re-ranking routine. Run the recursive R²CCL-AllReduce planner on a heterogeneous cluster where the recursion produces >=2 levels and where at least one inner sub-ring's node-skipping creates a rail-mismatch edge. Assert the re-ranking function is invoked once per recursion level, and that resulting rings satisfy the rail-overlap constraint at every level.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that launches the reduction (ReduceScatter/partial AllReduce) phases of all recursion-level rings in parallel to saturate bandwidth across the heterogeneous cluster.

verification.spec: Using a mocked/traced execution or CUDA-stream inspection, launch recursive R²CCL-AllReduce with >=2 recursion levels and assert that reduction-phase kernels/operations for all levels are issued concurrently (e.g., on different CUDA streams or NCCL channel groups) rather than serially. Verify by capturing launch timestamps that start times of the reduction phases overlap.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that enforces the broadcast-phase dependencies so that slower nodes correctly receive partial results from faster sub-rings, while allowing faster nodes' smaller broadcasts to overlap concurrently with slower ongoing operations.

verification.spec: In a simulated or emulated recursive AllReduce execution, verify: (1) slower nodes' broadcast receives block until the inner sub-ring's partial reduction completes (correctness dependency); (2) faster sub-rings' broadcasts can begin before slower ring broadcasts finish (overlap). Test by inserting artificial delays and asserting output correctness plus measured broadcast overlap.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that extends NCCL's α-β performance model to estimate expected completion time at each recursion depth, incorporating per-node bandwidth and inter-ring overlap.

verification.spec: Call the extended α-β cost model with (per-node bandwidths, message size, recursion depth d, overlap factor). Verify: (1) increasing recursion depth on a highly heterogeneous cluster reduces predicted time down to a minimum then increases (has a well-defined optimum); (2) the model returns finite non-negative time; (3) parameters α (link latency) and β (per-node bandwidth) both influence the output as expected (partial derivatives have correct sign).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for a planner that selects among standard Ring/Tree, R²CCL-Balance, and recursive R²CCL-AllReduce based on the α-β model's estimated completion time for the current failure configuration and message size.

verification.spec: Invoke the planner with three scenarios and assert selection: (a) homogeneous cluster, small message -> Ring/Tree; (b) single failure, small message (<32MB) -> R²CCL-Balance; (c) single failure, large message (>=512MB) -> R²CCL-AllReduce/recursive. Selection must be produced by comparing α-β-model estimates, not by hard-coded thresholds.

sub_tasks.requirements: The recursion produces correct AllReduce results: on a heterogeneous emulated cluster with three distinct per-node bandwidth tiers, every rank ends with byte-identical reduced output matching a reference AllReduce.

verification.spec: Set up an emulated cluster (e.g., 6 processes with gloo or NCCL on one node, or simulator) with three distinct per-node bandwidth tiers by throttling. Run recursive R²CCL-AllReduce over a randomly initialized float tensor and compare byte-for-byte (or bit-exact for integer / within FP tolerance 1e-6 for float sum) against a reference torch.distributed.all_reduce output on every rank.

sub_tasks.requirements: In the multi-failure Monte Carlo simulation with k concurrent failures distributed across 64 servers (512 GPUs) training the 7B model, R²CCL's average iteration-time overhead grows sub-linearly from approximately 1.5% at k=1 to approximately 4.3% at k=10 concurrent failures.

verification.spec: Reproduce Figure 10: using SimAI with 64 servers (512 A100 GPUs), 7B model training, randomly inject k concurrent NIC failures (k in {1,3,5,7,10}), 50 Monte Carlo runs per k. Report average iteration-time overhead vs. no-failure baseline. Verify overhead ~1.5% at k=1 and ~4.3% at k=10 with sub-linear growth.

sub_tasks.requirements: R²CCL is integrated as a ~3K LoC C++ extension to NCCL 2.23.4 with transport hooks, failover lists, planning-layer integration, and custom broadcast kernel.
R²CCL is packaged as a drop-in C++ extension to NCCL 2.23.4 that existing ML frameworks can use without modification.
Code has been implemented that builds R²CCL as an extension on top of NCCL version 2.23.4 (the exact version specified in Section 7).

verification.spec: Inspect the source tree / build metadata for a base NCCL version string equal to '2.23.4' (e.g., in nccl.h NCCL_MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH or in the vendored NCCL submodule tag/commit). Assert R²CCL builds against exactly NCCL 2.23.4.

sub_tasks.requirements: The R²CCL additions are implemented in C++ and are approximately 3,000 lines of code, forming an extension (not a fork rewrite) on top of the NCCL source tree.

verification.spec: Count non-comment, non-blank lines of C++ source added by R²CCL beyond the vanilla NCCL 2.23.4 baseline (e.g., using `cloc` on new/modified files with language=C++). Assert count is in the range approximately [2000, 4500] and that the code exists as additions/extensions rather than a full rewrite (base NCCL files largely unchanged).

sub_tasks.requirements: The library exposes the standard NCCL API (e.g., ncclCommInitRank, ncclAllReduce, ncclAllGather, ncclReduceScatter, ncclBroadcast, ncclSend/ncclRecv) so unmodified ML frameworks (PyTorch, vLLM) can link against it as a drop-in replacement.

verification.spec: Inspect the exported symbols of the built libnccl.so (e.g., via `nm -D` or `objdump -T`) and assert the presence of ncclCommInitRank, ncclAllReduce, ncclAllGather, ncclReduceScatter, ncclBroadcast, ncclSend, ncclRecv with matching signatures from nccl.h. Also verify SONAME is libnccl-compatible.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that provides a build system (e.g., Makefile / CMake) producing a libnccl.so-compatible shared library including all R²CCL extensions, linkable by PyTorch v2.10.0 and vLLM v1 as described in Section 8.1.

verification.spec: Run the R²CCL build system (make / cmake) from a clean checkout and verify it produces a shared library named libnccl.so (or a symlink chain) with the correct SONAME. Then LD_PRELOAD it (or set LD_LIBRARY_PATH) with a simple PyTorch v2.10.0 script that calls torch.distributed.init_process_group('nccl') and torch.distributed.all_reduce on a single-node 2-GPU config, and assert it completes successfully.

sub_tasks.requirements: R²CCL intercepts NCCL's communicator initialization at the ncclNet plugin layer to establish backup RDMA connections and multi-NIC GPU buffer registrations.
Code has been implemented that hooks the ncclNet plugin layer during ncclCommInitRank to intercept transport-layer connection setup and extend it with R²CCL's backup path logic.

verification.spec: Grep the source for hooks registered against the ncclNet plugin API (ncclNet_v* struct: init, listen, connect, accept, regMr, etc.) and verify R²CCL overrides or wraps these entry points to establish backup connections during ncclCommInitRank. Assert calls to backup-path setup functions from within the ncclNet init/connect code path.

sub_tasks.requirements: The memory registration path is extended so that each GPU buffer used by a communicator is registered with all local NICs of the server at communicator initialization time (multi-NIC GPU buffer registration).

verification.spec: Instrument the memory-registration path (regMr) to log which (buffer, NIC) pairs are registered during ncclCommInitRank. Run a two-node communicator init with 4+ NICs per node and assert that for every registered GPU buffer, an ibv_reg_mr (or equivalent) is issued against every local NIC of the server, not just one.

sub_tasks.requirements: Connection setup logic has been extended to create additional RDMA queue pairs over backup NICs (idle 'sleep' connections) in addition to the primary connection during bootstrap.

verification.spec: During ncclCommInitRank bootstrap on 2 nodes with N NICs each, capture the QP-creation calls (ibv_create_qp). Assert that for each channel, in addition to the primary QP on the assigned NIC, at least one additional QP is created against each backup NIC and transitioned to RTR/RTS (or an equivalently 'connected but idle' state), forming the sleep-connection pool.

sub_tasks.requirements: Backup connection handles are organized into a per-channel failover list ordered by PCIe distance to the source GPU, so that failure recovery selects the topologically closest healthy NIC first.

verification.spec: For a channel bound to source GPU g, query the failover list data structure after ncclCommInitRank and assert its ordering matches non-decreasing PCIe distance from g to each candidate NIC (using topology data from nvidia-smi topo -m or NCCL's XML topology). Test on ≥2 GPU-NIC configurations.

sub_tasks.requirements: Multi-registration is performed only at initialization time and reuses mapping entries at failover (no on-demand re-registration in the recovery path), so live-migration latency remains in the low-millisecond range rather than the millisecond-per-buffer / tens-of-milliseconds cost of on-demand registration.

verification.spec: Instrument the failover code path to count ibv_reg_mr / cudaHostRegister calls made during a live migration event. Trigger a NIC failure mid-AllReduce and assert zero new memory-registration calls occur on the recovery path. Additionally, measure end-to-end live-migration latency (from OOB failure notification receipt to first retransmitted chunk on backup NIC) and assert it is under 10 ms.

sub_tasks.requirements: The InfiniBand net plugin and proxy send/receive progress loops are modified to detect failures, avoid crashing, roll back, and reissue chunks on backup connections.
The modified InfiniBand plugin monitors RDMA Completion Queue (CQ) and Queue Pair (QP) errors and reports them as failed requests to the NCCL proxy rather than aborting the process.

verification.spec: Inject a synthetic RDMA CQ error (e.g., via a mock ibv_poll_cq returning IBV_WC_RETRY_EXC_ERR or QP transition to error state) during a running AllReduce and verify: (1) the process does not abort/crash; (2) the plugin reports a failed request to the NCCL proxy; (3) the proxy invokes the R²CCL recovery path. Test with both CQ-completion errors and QP-async errors.

sub_tasks.requirements: The net plugin and proxy send/receive progress loops are augmented to catch RDMA transport / QP-level errors and prevent the application process from crashing on connection errors during a collective.

verification.spec: Inspect the modified NCCL net plugin (ncclNet) and proxy send/recv progress loops for handlers that catch CQ/QP errors (e.g., IBV_WC_RETRY_EXC_ERR, IBV_WC_WR_FLUSH_ERR). Run a two-node NCCL test with an injected RDMA transport error mid-collective and verify the application process does not crash (exit code != SIGABRT/SIGSEGV) and reports the error via the plugin path rather than aborting.

sub_tasks.requirements: Upon confirmed failure, the proxy rolls the affected channel back to the last chunk with a confirmed work-completion, purges outstanding work requests, transitions the channel to the next backup connection, and reissues the remaining chunks over it.

verification.spec: Instrument the proxy rollback logic and run a controlled test: transmit a multi-chunk RDMA send, inject failure after N chunks are acknowledged, then verify (via log output or unit-test harness) that (a) the channel rewinds to chunk N (last confirmed completion), (b) outstanding work requests on the failed QP are purged, (c) the channel switches to the next backup NIC, and (d) chunks N+1..end are reissued. Compare final received buffer against expected data byte-for-byte.

sub_tasks.requirements: R²CCL-Balance and R²CCL-AllReduce are integrated into NCCL's enqueue/planning logic to select and configure failure-aware schedules.

R²CCL-Balance is integrated into NCCL's enqueue and planning logic so that, before an algorithm is selected and rings/trees are instantiated, the planner inspects per-NIC health status records for each node.

verification.spec: Inspect NCCL enqueue/planning code paths (ncclEnqueue, ncclTopoCompute*) for R2CCL modifications that consult a per-node per-NIC health status structure prior to algorithm selection and ring/tree instantiation. Verify via a unit test that toggling a NIC's health flag changes the planner's channel-to-NIC assignment before an algorithm is chosen.

sub_tasks.requirements: The planner redistributes channels that would have used a failed NIC across the remaining healthy NICs on the same node in proportion to their available bandwidth.

verification.spec: Unit-test the planner: create a mock node with N NICs of known bandwidths, mark one NIC as failed, and verify the planner redistributes the channels of the failed NIC across remaining NICs with per-NIC channel counts proportional (within 1 channel of ideal) to their available bandwidths. Also verify total data assigned to node is unchanged.

sub_tasks.requirements: R²CCL-AllReduce uses NCCL's channel abstraction to partition channels into two concurrent groups in the first stage: one running a global AllReduce across all nodes and one running a partial AllReduce that excludes the degraded node.

verification.spec: Run R2CCL-AllReduce with a simulated degraded node and log channel assignments during phase 1. Verify two disjoint channel groups exist: group A includes all ranks (global AllReduce), group B excludes the degraded node ranks (partial AllReduce). Verify both groups launch concurrently (overlapping timestamps on kernel start) and process disjoint data shards.

sub_tasks.requirements: A runtime strategy selector uses an α–β performance model (parameterized by machine-specific link latency α and bandwidth β from NCCL) together with the operation's data size to choose among standard Ring/Tree, R²CCL-Balance, and R²CCL-AllReduce (including recursive R²CCL-AllReduce) rather than a fixed threshold.

verification.spec: Exercise the strategy selector via a test harness that supplies varied (data_size, alpha, beta, failure_fraction X) inputs and verify: (i) small messages select Ring/Tree or R2CCL-Balance, (ii) large messages with X>=1/3 select R2CCL-AllReduce, (iii) multi-failure scenarios select recursive R2CCL-AllReduce. Confirm decisions are computed via the alpha-beta model (not a hardcoded size threshold) by varying alpha/beta and observing crossover changes.

sub_tasks.requirements: A custom CUDA broadcast kernel implements the second-stage delivery of the partial-AllReduce result to the degraded node in R²CCL-AllReduce.
Code has been implemented that provides a custom CUDA broadcast kernel dedicated to the R²CCL-AllReduce second phase (i.e., not reusing an unmodified stock NCCL broadcast kernel).

verification.spec: Locate a custom CUDA broadcast kernel (.cu file) in the R2CCL source tree that is invoked specifically during the R2CCL-AllReduce second phase. Confirm it is not merely a call into stock ncclBroadcast by inspecting the launch site and kernel signature; check that the kernel name/symbol is distinct from NCCL's built-in broadcast kernels.

sub_tasks.requirements: The second-stage broadcast implements the three-part schedule described in Section 5.2: (i) a broadcast initiated from the failure server node, (ii) a pipelined ring broadcast across the healthy servers, and (iii) delivery of the partial-AllReduce result from the last ring node back to the failure node, so that all servers obtain the full correct AllReduce result.

verification.spec: Trace the R2CCL-AllReduce second stage execution on a 4+ node setup with one degraded node. Confirm three ordered sub-operations: (i) a broadcast originating from the degraded node to healthy nodes, (ii) a pipelined ring broadcast among healthy nodes, (iii) a final send from the last healthy ring node delivering the partial-AllReduce result back to the degraded node. Verify by kernel launch logs and final buffer correctness on all ranks.

sub_tasks.requirements: The integrated implementation achieves the headline overheads reported in the paper, verifying that transport hooks, planning integration, and the custom kernel work together end-to-end.

With the integrated R²CCL library plugged into unmodified PyTorch v2.10.0 + Megatron-LM, a single injected NIC failure produces less than 1% end-to-end training throughput overhead relative to the no-failure baseline (as claimed as the headline number for training in the abstract and Section 8).

verification.spec: Run Megatron-LM GPT-3 2.7B with DP=16 on two 8xH100 nodes using PyTorch 2.10.0 linked against R2CCL. Measure tokens/s over a stable window without failure, then with one NIC failure injected mid-training. Compute overhead = (baseline - failure) / baseline. Expect <1% overhead with R2CCL-AllReduce.

sub_tasks.requirements: With the integrated R²CCL library plugged into unmodified vLLM v1, a single injected NIC failure produces less than 3% end-to-end inference overhead relative to the no-failure baseline (headline inference number).

verification.spec: Run vLLM v1 with TP=8,PP=2 on two 8xH100 nodes serving Llama-3.1-405B (or a comparable large model) using R2CCL. Measure TTFT (or TPOT) at a fixed QPS in no-failure and single-NIC-failure conditions. Compute overhead = (failure - baseline) / baseline. Expect <3%.
