sub_tasks.requirements: Megatron-LM GPT-3 2.7B (DP=16) and 13B (TP=8, PP=2) training under single and dual NIC failures reproduces the reported <1% overhead and comparisons to vanilla NCCL and AdapCC on the two-node H100 physical testbed.
Training workload harness for GPT-3 2.7B and 13B via Megatron-LM is set up on the two-node H100 testbed.

Code has been implemented to launch Megatron-LM GPT-3 2.7B training with DP=16 (16 GPUs across the two 8xH100 nodes), producing an executable training script with the exact parallelism configuration used in Section 8.2.

verification.spec: Verify a launchable Megatron-LM training script exists with parallelism arguments: --tensor-model-parallel-size 1 --pipeline-model-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 16, targeting GPT-3 2.7B (hidden_size=2560, layers=32, num_heads=32) on 2x8 H100 nodes. Do a dry-run (--exit-interval 1) to confirm the config is accepted.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to launch Megatron-LM GPT-3 13B training with TP=8, PP=2 spanning the two nodes such that pipeline stages induce inter-node point-to-point activations.

verification.spec: Verify a launchable Megatron-LM training script exists with --tensor-model-parallel-size 8 --pipeline-model-parallel-size 2 for GPT-3 13B on the two-node 8xH100 testbed. Confirm pipeline stages are placed on different nodes (rank-to-node mapping shows PP boundaries at inter-node links) via a dry-run.

sub_tasks.requirements: The training harness uses PyTorch v2.10.0 compiled against NCCL v2.23.4 (and R2CCL) as described in Section 8.1, and the linked NCCL library is verifiable at runtime.

verification.spec: At training runtime, log torch.__version__ (expect 2.10.0) and torch.cuda.nccl.version() plus the loaded libnccl.so path. Verify the linked NCCL is either the vendored R2CCL-modified 2.23.4 or unmodified 2.23.4 depending on config, by inspecting build metadata or presence of R2CCL symbols (e.g., nm libnccl.so | grep r2ccl).

sub_tasks.requirements: NVIDIA SHARP is explicitly disabled in the training runs (per Section 8.1 footnote) so that reported collective performance is not augmented by in-network reduction.

verification.spec: Verify environment variable NCCL_ALGO does not include NVLS/NVLS_TREE and/or NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0 is set (or SHARP is not built in). Check NCCL debug logs (NCCL_DEBUG=INFO) for absence of 'SHARP' or 'NVLS' selection lines during collective execution.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to record training throughput in tokens/second, averaged over a stable window that excludes warm-up iterations, matching the reporting used in Figure 7.

verification.spec: Verify the training harness logs tokens/second per iteration and computes an averaged tokens/s that explicitly skips the first K warm-up iterations (K>=10). Confirm by inspecting logging code and running a short training job to see per-iteration and windowed averaged output.

sub_tasks.requirements: NIC failure injection mechanism supports single and dual NIC faults on one node during running collectives.
Code has been implemented to inject a single NIC failure (12.5% bandwidth loss) on one of the two H100 nodes during ongoing training, simulating a hardware-visible transport error.

verification.spec: Run a fault-injection tool (e.g., `ibdev2netdev` + `ip link set <nic> down` or MLX diagnostic to disable one InfiniBand port) on one H100 node during an active Megatron-LM training run. Verify (i) the NIC becomes unavailable in `ibv_devinfo`, (ii) R2CCL logs detect the failure within ~milliseconds via bilateral notification, and (iii) training continues (does not abort). 12.5% bandwidth loss = 1/8 NICs.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to inject two concurrent NIC failures on a single node for the dual-failure R2CCL-Two-Failures configuration reported in Section 8.2.

verification.spec: Extend the single-NIC injection tool to bring down 2 InfiniBand ports simultaneously on one node during training. Verify both are marked failed, R2CCL migrates traffic, and training continues without abort.

sub_tasks.requirements: Failure injection is timed so that faults occur mid-collective (during an active AllReduce or P2P transfer), verifying that R2CCL exercises the in-flight failover path rather than a between-collective reconfiguration.

verification.spec: Instrument the fault injector to trigger during an active AllReduce/P2P (e.g., via a hook that observes ncclKernel launch and triggers link-down mid-kernel). Verify from R2CCL logs that the recovery path taken is the in-flight failover (rollback+retransmit on backup NIC) rather than a between-collective reconfigure (i.e., failure timestamp falls between kernel start and end, and recovery does not require ncclCommInitRank re-invocation).

sub_tasks.requirements: Baseline configurations for the physical training comparison are implemented and runnable.
Vanilla NCCL 2.23.4 baseline is set up unmodified and expected to crash on injected NIC failure, reproducing the 'complete failure' outcome for DP=16 GPT-3 2.7B training.

verification.spec: Configure the exact same GPT-3 2.7B DP=16 training with unmodified NCCL 2.23.4 (not R2CCL). Inject a NIC failure mid-training and verify the process aborts (non-zero exit, tokens/s drops to 0). Log the crash traceback to confirm NCCL raised a fatal error.

sub_tasks.requirements: AdapCC baseline is set up per Zhao et al. 2024 for GPT-3 2.7B DP=16, excluding failed GPUs from subsequent collectives while remaining ranks continue training.

verification.spec: Build/install AdapCC (Zhao et al. 2024) per its public release. Launch GPT-3 2.7B DP=16 on the two-node 8xH100 testbed using AdapCC as the collective backend. Inject a NIC failure before a collective and verify (i) the affected ranks are excluded, (ii) remaining ranks continue training, (iii) tokens/s is measured and reflects the ~8.65% overhead reported in the paper.

sub_tasks.requirements: For TP=8, PP=2 on the 13B model, the AdapCC configuration is exercised and its inability to operate under rank exclusion (0 tokens/s outcome) is captured, matching the paper's observation that removing a rank violates TP/PP partitioning constraints.

verification.spec: Launch Megatron-LM GPT-3 13B with TP=8, PP=2 using AdapCC. Inject a NIC failure and verify AdapCC's rank-exclusion strategy causes the job to fail to produce tokens (0 tokens/s) because TP/PP world sizes require a fixed rank count. Log the failure mode.

sub_tasks.requirements: R2CCL variants R2CCL-HotRepair, R2CCL-Balance, and R2CCL-AllReduce are each independently selectable at runtime so that all three configurations in Figure 7 can be measured on the same training setup.

verification.spec: Verify an environment variable or config flag (e.g., R2CCL_STRATEGY={HOTREPAIR,BALANCE,ALLREDUCE}) selects among the three R2CCL variants at runtime. Launch three identical training runs differing only in this flag and confirm from R2CCL debug logs that the selected strategy matches the flag.

sub_tasks.requirements: Under a single NIC failure, DP=16 GPT-3 2.7B training numerically reproduces the throughput and overhead values in Figure 7.
No-failure baseline throughput for GPT-3 2.7B DP=16 measures approximately 314,618 tokens/s, matching the reference value reported in Section 8.2.

verification.spec: Run GPT-3 2.7B DP=16 with vanilla NCCL 2.23.4 (no failures) on 2x8 H100 nodes and measure steady-state tokens/s over >=100 iterations after warm-up.

sub_tasks.requirements: Under single NIC failure with R2CCL-AllReduce, GPT-3 2.7B DP=16 sustains approximately 312,394 tokens/s, corresponding to about 0.71% overhead versus the no-failure baseline.

verification.spec: Run GPT-3 2.7B DP=16 with R2CCL-AllReduce and one NIC failure injected on one H100 node. Measure tokens/s over a stable window and report the value.

sub_tasks.requirements: Under single NIC failure with R2CCL-Balance, GPT-3 2.7B DP=16 training incurs approximately 1.32% overhead relative to the no-failure baseline.

verification.spec: Run GPT-3 2.7B DP=16 with R2CCL-Balance and one NIC failure injected. Measure tokens/s and compute overhead = (baseline - failure)/baseline * 100 using the same baseline as the no-failure run. Expect ~1.32%.

sub_tasks.requirements: Under single NIC failure with R2CCL-HotRepair, GPT-3 2.7B DP=16 training incurs approximately 4.82% overhead relative to the no-failure baseline.

verification.spec: Run Megatron-LM GPT-3 2.7B with DP=16 on the 2-node 8xH100 testbed using R2CCL-HotRepair. Measure tokens/s under a single NIC failure injected mid-run and compare to the no-failure baseline (~314,618 tokens/s). Compute overhead = (baseline - measured)/baseline and verify approximately 4.82%.

sub_tasks.requirements: AdapCC on GPT-3 2.7B DP=16 under single NIC failure exhibits approximately 8.65% overhead, matching the paper's report that AdapCC has the worst slowdown due to reduced compute capacity.

verification.spec: Run Megatron-LM GPT-3 2.7B with DP=16 under AdapCC on the 2-node 8xH100 testbed with a single NIC failure injected. Measure tokens/s and compute overhead versus the ~314,618 tokens/s no-failure baseline; verify approximately 8.65%.

sub_tasks.requirements: Under a single NIC failure, GPT-3 13B TP=8, PP=2 training numerically reproduces the throughput and overhead values in Figure 7.
No-failure baseline throughput for GPT-3 13B TP=8, PP=2 measures approximately 8,340 tokens/s, matching the reference value reported in Section 8.2.

verification.spec: Run Megatron-LM GPT-3 13B with TP=8, PP=2 on the 2-node 8xH100 testbed using vanilla NCCL without any failure injection. Measure sustained tokens/s and verify it is approximately 8,340.

sub_tasks.requirements: Under single NIC failure with R2CCL-Balance, GPT-3 13B TP=8, PP=2 sustains approximately 8,309 tokens/s, corresponding to about 0.38% overhead relative to the no-failure baseline.

verification.spec: Run Megatron-LM GPT-3 13B with TP=8, PP=2 on the 2-node 8xH100 testbed using R2CCL-Balance with a single NIC failure injected. Measure sustained tokens/s and verify it is ~8,309 (i.e., ~0.38% overhead vs ~8,340 baseline).

sub_tasks.requirements: Under single NIC failure with R2CCL-HotRepair, GPT-3 13B TP=8, PP=2 training incurs approximately 1.31% overhead relative to the no-failure baseline.

verification.spec: Run Megatron-LM GPT-3 13B with TP=8, PP=2 on the 2-node 8xH100 testbed using R2CCL-HotRepair with a single NIC failure injected. Compute overhead vs the ~8,340 tokens/s no-failure baseline and verify approximately 1.31%.

sub_tasks.requirements: AdapCC on GPT-3 13B TP=8, PP=2 under single NIC failure yields 0 tokens/s (job cannot proceed), confirming AdapCC's incompatibility with TP/PP partitioning constraints on this workload.

verification.spec: Run Megatron-LM GPT-3 13B with TP=8, PP=2 under AdapCC on the 2-node 8xH100 testbed with a single NIC failure. Verify that AdapCC cannot proceed (0 tokens/s) because excluding a rank violates TP/PP partitioning constraints; the job either fails to launch or produces no training tokens.

sub_tasks.requirements: Under two simultaneous NIC failures on one node, both training configurations retain near-baseline throughput as claimed in Section 8.2.
With two concurrent NIC failures on one node during GPT-3 2.7B DP=16 training, R2CCL sustains approximately 310,756 tokens/s, corresponding to about 1.24% overhead versus the no-failure baseline.

verification.spec: Run Megatron-LM GPT-3 2.7B DP=16 on the 2-node H100 testbed with R2CCL and inject two simultaneous NIC failures on one node. Measure sustained tokens/s and verify it is approximately 310,756 (i.e., ~1.24% overhead vs ~314,618 baseline).

sub_tasks.requirements: With two concurrent NIC failures on one node during GPT-3 13B TP=8, PP=2 training, R2CCL sustains approximately 8,257 tokens/s, corresponding to about 1.01% overhead versus the no-failure baseline.

verification.spec: Run Megatron-LM GPT-3 13B TP=8, PP=2 on the 2-node H100 testbed with R2CCL and inject two concurrent NIC failures on one node. Measure sustained tokens/s and verify ~8,257 (i.e., ~1.01% overhead vs ~8,340 baseline).

sub_tasks.requirements: Aggregate comparative claims across all physical-testbed training configurations hold.

sub_tasks.requirements: Three inference configurations under comparison (non-fault-tolerant baseline, DéjàVu with vanilla NCCL, DéjàVu with R²CCL) are built and exercised correctly.
Code has been implemented to build DéjàVu (per Strati et al., 2024b) linked against vanilla NCCL v2.23.4 with KV-cache replication enabled as its native fault-tolerance mechanism.

verification.spec: Build DejaVu from source linked against NCCL v2.23.4. Confirm build succeeds, ldd on the DejaVu binary/lib shows libnccl.so v2.23.4, and KV-cache replication is enabled by default config. Run a short inference smoke test with KV replication logs printed.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to build DéjàVu with R²CCL substituted in place of NCCL at the collective communication layer, without modifying DéjàVu application code.

verification.spec: Build DejaVu against R2CCL (drop-in replace libnccl.so with R2CCL library). Verify: (a) build succeeds without modifying DejaVu source (git diff on DejaVu dir shows no application code changes); (b) ldd shows R2CCL library linked; (c) short inference smoke test passes.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to run a non-fault-tolerant baseline that reprocesses the full request after the injected failure, serving as the reference for the 1.62× / 1.79× baseline latency inflation.

verification.spec: Verify the non-fault-tolerant baseline: NCCL-linked vLLM/inference stack that, on NIC failure, restarts the request from scratch (full prefill+decode reprocessed). Trigger a failure mid-request and confirm from logs that the request is reprocessed from token 0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The R²CCL-integrated DéjàVu run performs transparent connection migration on failure, resuming decoding without triggering DéjàVu's KV-cache reconstruction path or a worker restart.

verification.spec: Run DejaVu+R2CCL with a NIC failure injected at decode step 800. Inspect logs to assert: (a) no worker restart occurred, (b) DejaVu's KV-cache reconstruction/replication-recovery path was NOT invoked, (c) R2CCL migration path was triggered and decoding resumed on the backup NIC without gap in step numbering.

sub_tasks.requirements: Measurement and metric-reporting logic reproduces the single-request cumulative latency methodology of DéjàVu.

verification.spec: Run single-request generation and verify the harness produces a CSV/JSON with 1500 rows containing per-decode-step cumulative latency. Confirm the harness can render curves equivalent to Figure 14 (cumulative latency vs decode step) for each of the three systems.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to compute recovery-overhead ratios (final cumulative latency relative to the no-failure run) for each of the three systems on each model.

verification.spec: Verify script that takes cumulative-latency logs for the three systems (non-FT, DejaVu, R2CCL) and no-failure baseline and computes overhead ratio = final_latency_with_failure / final_latency_no_failure per system per model. Run on sample logs and confirm expected numerical outputs.

sub_tasks.requirements: For BLOOM-176B, the non-fault-tolerant baseline exhibits cumulative-latency inflation of approximately 1.79× relative to the no-failure run after the failure injected at decode step 800.

The function returns the optimized ring R'.

verification.spec: Import the re-ranking function. Construct a small ring of 4-6 nodes with rail sets designed so exactly one adjacent pair (u,v) has |S_u ∩ S_v| < Bglobal, and some non-adjacent node w satisfies min(|S_u∩S_w|,|S_w∩S_v|) >= Bglobal while |S_prev(w) ∩ S_next(w)| >= Bglobal. Assert output ring places w between u and v. Also test: (a) if no pair violates threshold, ring is unchanged; (b) candidate pairs are processed in descending gap-size order (verify via a two-violation setup where processing order matters); (c) if no valid bridge exists, the offending pair is left in place.
verification.paper_cite: Section 6 (Topology-Aware Logical Re-ranking) and Appendix pseudocode

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that a recursive dual-ring decomposition scheduler peels off sub-rings by bandwidth tier: given per-node available bandwidths, it forms a global ring at the slowest node's rate, isolates that node, forms a faster sub-ring on the remaining nodes, and recursively continues as long as bandwidth variance persists. Each ring is assigned a data chunk proportional to the incremental bandwidth of its members, and logical re-ranking is applied at every level.

verification.spec: Import the recursive decomposition planner. Feed a synthetic cluster with 4 bandwidth tiers (e.g., bandwidths [1.0, 1.0, 0.5, 0.25] per node). Assert: (1) the returned schedule contains a global ring including all nodes; (2) at least one sub-ring excludes the slowest node; (3) further sub-rings peel off the next-slowest node when bandwidth variance among the remainder exceeds a tolerance; (4) sum of per-ring data chunks equals total data size D within 1e-6; (5) each ring's chunk size is proportional to the incremental bandwidth of its members (verify ratios). Also test that a homogeneous-bandwidth input produces a single ring (no recursion).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the recursive R2CCL-AllReduce executes the reduction phases of all rings in parallel while enforcing dependency-aware broadcast scheduling: slower nodes' broadcasts wait for partial results from faster sub-rings, and faster nodes may execute their (smaller) broadcasts concurrently with slower nodes' ongoing operations.

verification.spec: Import the scheduler that emits an execution plan (list of (phase, ring_id, op_type, dependencies)). For a 3-tier decomposition, assert: (1) all reduction-phase entries have no cross-ring dependencies (they run in parallel); (2) each broadcast-phase entry on a slower ring lists a dependency on the completed partial-AllReduce result of the corresponding faster sub-ring; (3) broadcast entries for faster (smaller) sub-rings have no dependency on slower rings' broadcast completion, allowing concurrency. Verify by topological-sort simulation that total simulated completion time is strictly less than the sequential sum, confirming overlap.
verification.paper_cite: Section 6 (Recursive R2CCL-AllReduce, parallel reduction + dependency-aware broadcast)

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that an alpha-beta performance model planner evaluates expected completion time at each recursion depth (incorporating per-node bandwidth and overlap) and selects among standard Ring/Tree, R2CCL-Balance, or recursive R2CCL-AllReduce for a given collective invocation.

verification.spec: Import the planner. Feed configurations where the correct choice is known analytically: (1) tiny message size + homogeneous bandwidth -> planner selects Ring or Tree (latency-bound); (2) large message + single-NIC failure with lost-bandwidth fraction X in [1/3, 1) -> selects recursive R2CCL-AllReduce (per Section 5.2 threshold ng/(3ng-2)); (3) large message + single failure with X < 1/3 -> selects standard Ring; (4) non-AllReduce collective (e.g., AllGather) under failure -> selects R2CCL-Balance. Verify that the planner uses NCCL-provided per-link alpha and beta parameters as inputs (function signature accepts them) and that predicted completion time for the chosen strategy is the minimum among evaluated options.
verification.paper_cite: Section 6 (alpha-beta planner) and Section 5.2 threshold analysis

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements a data-partition solver that, given the lost-bandwidth fraction X on the failure node, number of servers n, GPUs per server g, healthy-node bandwidth B, and total data size D, computes the optimal fraction Y of data assigned to the partial AllReduce by minimizing T_total(Y) = max(T1(Y), T2(Y)) + T3(Y), where T1(Y) = 2(ng-1)/(ng) * ((1-Y)/(1-X)) * D/B, T2(Y) = 2((n-1)g-1)/((n-1)g) * YD/(XB), T3(Y) = YD/(XB)

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements a runtime alpha-beta model that, given message size D, lost-bandwidth fraction X, and per-link (alpha, beta) parameters, selects among {Ring, R2CCL-Balance, R2CCL-AllReduce} to minimize predicted completion time. In particular, the selector must return Ring when 0 < X < 1/3 and R2CCL-AllReduce when 1/3 <= X < 1 for throughput-bound (large D) inputs, and prefer R2CCL-Balance for small messages (<32MB) where AllReduce coordination overhead dominates

Invoke the scheduler's plan/execute function and inspect the emitted schedule (e.g., list of (ring_id, phase, start_time, end_time) tuples or channel assignments). Assert that for the reduction phase of every ring, at least two rings have overlapping [start_time, end_time) intervals (i.e., they are scheduled concurrently on distinct channels), and that no reduction phase is gated on the completion of another ring's reduction phase.
verification.paper_cite: Section 6, 'R2CCL executes the reduction phases of all rings in parallel to saturate available bandwidth.'

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that broadcast phases in recursive R2CCL-AllReduce enforce dependencies: slower nodes wait for partial AllReduce results from faster sub-rings before completing their broadcast, while allowing faster sub-rings to overlap their broadcasts with slower nodes' ongoing operations where bandwidth permits.

verification.spec: Construct a 3-tier bandwidth scenario (1 slow node, 1 medium node, remaining fast nodes) so the scheduler emits >=2 sub-rings. Invoke the planner and inspect the resulting schedule DAG. Assert (a) the slow node's broadcast phase has an explicit dependency edge on the completion of at least one faster sub-ring's partial-AllReduce result, and (b) the faster sub-ring's broadcast phase is scheduled to start before the slow node's broadcast completes (overlap). Fail if broadcasts are fully serialized or if slow-node broadcast starts before receiving fast sub-ring partial.
verification.paper_cite: Section 6, 'Broadcast phases impose dependencies—slower nodes must wait for partial results from faster sub-rings—but bandwidth asymmetry often allows faster nodes to finish their smaller broadcasts concurrently with slower nodes' ongoing operations.'

Also verify the cost formula reads per-node bandwidth (not just cluster-wide bandwidth) and includes an overlap term.
verification.paper_cite: Section 6, 'R2CCL extends NCCL's performance model (α–β) to evaluate expected completion time at each recursion depth ... The planner then selects among standard Ring/Tree, R2CCL-Balance, or recursive R2CCL-AllReduce.'
